steps.name: Lena
steps.text: Medication and suppressants that need to be administered on a regular basis, fresh from the Rhodes Island office.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: I heard the Astynomos' Office has lifted the detention order on Xanthos and his apprentice, and does not intend to press charges against you for helping them escape.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Yes. I learned later that Lydia had guessed our plan and intentionally made things easy for me. Stands to reason she wouldn't pursue the matter.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: But the three of you still intend to leave Athenius?

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Staying will only give my old classmate ideas. He needs to see more places, meet more people, do more things.

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: I rarely see you so honest, Lykeion. I wouldn't have had three operators keep an eye on you, if you were like this when you were my patient.

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: Sorry for the trouble I caused...

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Looks like Xanthos's actions at the First Temple had a considerable influence on you.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: How about you wave the white flag and admit that Oripathy doesn't sap the heroic spirit at all?

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: In your dreams.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Talk about a hardhead.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: You should go, or you'll miss the ferry. Xanthos's substitute is not as flexible about late passengers. He won't wait for you.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Skata! Let's go, Lykeion.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Thank you for the medicine, Kyría Athopoulou. May we meet again!

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: Hey, stay off the lawn! I just worked on it—

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: Well, I suppose two young men won't be nearly as destructive as a whole herd of burdenbeasts.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: The flowers and grass they ruined haven't been cleaned up yet. Too bad about the blue boronia...

steps.name: Young Lena
steps.text: Don't cry, Lydia...

steps.name: Young Lydia
steps.text: If bad guys ruin your house like they ruined my old home...

steps.name: Young Lydia
steps.text: We won't have a home to go back to. What would we do?

steps.name: Young Lena
steps.text: Don't worry. I'll never leave you behind, even if the house is gone, even if we're separated!

steps.name: Young Lena
steps.text: I know! Look for this garden if you're far away from home and don't know the way back.

steps.name: Young Lydia
steps.text: Garden...?

steps.name: Young Lena
steps.text: Yeah! I'll plant blue boronia here, so that you'll know you're home when you see it.

steps.name: Young Lena
steps.text: And if you find the way first, mark it the same way, won't you?

steps.name: Young Lydia
steps.text: Alright... it's a promise, Lena.
The public garden's lawn, once filled with flowers and herbs, is now filled only with burdenbeast footprints.
Even if it has temporarily lost its beauty, however, the blue petals remain in the soil.

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: So many blue boronias... you think of the past too, don't you?

steps.name: Lena
steps.text: Thank you, Lydia. I'm home.

steps.name: Fruit Farmer Rep
steps.text: I brought this year's apples, Kassandra!

steps.name: Fruit Farmer Rep
steps.text: The portion set aside for the temple's offering has been sent to the cellar. I saved this for you and the others at the temple to share.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Thank you. It's very kind of you, to do it every year.

steps.name: Fruit Farmer Rep
steps.text: Our good harvests are all thanks to the help of everyone in Athenius. Besides, you helped so much with coordinating the temple.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: You seem to be in a good mood today.

steps.name: Fruit Farmer Rep
steps.text: To us, nothing matters more than the harvest, and a good harvest brings happiness.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Nothing matters to us more than everybody's happiness, and the harvest is an important part of it.

spans.text: more than everybody's happiness, and the harvest is an important part of it.

steps.name: Fruit Farmer Rep
steps.text: We're counting on you! I'll take my leave now. The pomegranate will be ripe for harvest soon, and there are branches waiting to be trimmed.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Sweet apples and bright sun. What a lovely day!

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: The ceremony at the First Temple was successfully concluded, and the ferryman that you were caring for has found hope.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: All is well, isn't it, Hiéreia? Why do you look so sullen?

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: You're the one I'm worried about.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Me? Why?

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: I've been thinking about what you said when you came back to Athenius.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: You said you saw the beginnings of Minos in your dreams, saw Kereseira and her First Temple.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: You said you thought a lot about Minos's past and future, about your own goals and direction.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: All this is why you came back.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: The events of recent days seem to corroborate my interpretation of the divine revelation. It is not a beautiful future of smiles and flowers. The unease lingers in my heart.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Divine revelation is simply the direction that the spirit of heroes has shown us. It is not an inevitable future. We learned about that in priest school.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: That's true for ordinary revelations, but...

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: For example, I wanted the harp to return, but the peculiar manner of its return makes it seem so inevitable and unchangeable...

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Look at it from a different perspective. While the final goal was the return of the harp, the manner of its return was wondrous. Perhaps it's the same for my revelation.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Or perhaps, your interpretation is not the final goal. It's only one of the trials during the process, and the goal lies elsewhere.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: ...I hope you're right.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Besides, the recent events have demonstrated that it was right for me to come back. Minos needs me, and I need it.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: But you don't want to take over the First Temple, despite the fact that the bulk of the work is done.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Is it because you believe your Oripathy will be an obstacle to priesthood? But Xanthos has told me about the vision he saw on the temple square. I thought you didn't worry anymore.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Traditions can be changed. You were right. I can initiate a vote at the council...

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: No, I didn't propose rebuilding the First Temple to become its priestess.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: I wanted to unite our spirit, not just Athenians, but other city-states and Minoans too...

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: I heard Lachedamon and Corinia have changed a lot. I want to see them for myself.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: So you did come to say goodbye.

steps.name: Pallas
steps.text: Not quite yet. I want to see the temple project through to the end. I'm not missing the completion party that Kantia is already planning!

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Carefree as always.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: Thank you for the kind invitation. It was quite an unexpected play.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: Athenius is about to depart along its planned route, and it's time for us to depart as well.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: I hope you will excuse the unpredictable events that occurred. It seems I did not plan for every possible contingency.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: On this, there is something I'm curious about.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: The ferryman openly accused you of making secret deals with the Sargonians on the temple square, and you were summoned to the council yesterday for an emergency hearing.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: Yet you are back in your office, safe and sound. Did you have a trump card up your sleeve? Or is there more to this matter than meets the eye?

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: More than meets the eye' is overstating it. I had simply made certain arrangements for the follow-up to this matter. The council heard the explanation and is satisfied that I remain competent to govern.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: As for the details, I regret that I am unable to share them as yet. They will reveal themselves in due time.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: All we need to know is that you remain the Astynomos of Athenius.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: With sweeping authority over major matters of administration and governance.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: I'm glad to hear it. And now, I have a formal proposal to make.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: I'm sure both of you understand that dramatic changes are happening in Minos right now.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: It is the case in Athenius, and it is the case in Lachedamon, where a new arena is being built, one that will host competitors from far and wide.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: Perhaps the word 'tradition' is not quite music to your ears, Astynomos, but don't you think that now is the time for us to revive the old traditions?

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: Changes are happening across the land. How about the Three Poleis set aside their rivalries, return to the old city-state federation, and revive an ancient festival?

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: The scattered villages and minor poleis will surely answer the call, and the nation will grow stronger.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: It will be the perfect opportunity, to restore Minos's glory, and to spread the sacred flame across the land.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: What do you think?

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: Is this why you've been snooping around Athenius? You were investigating us.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: Old merchant habits die hard. Can't go into the market without doing research. I apologize if I caused any offense.

steps.name: Lydia
steps.text: You're good at causing accidents. I'm afraid I can't give you an answer right now.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: That's not a problem. It's right to be prudent.

steps.name: Períandros
steps.text: What about you, priestess Cynisca of Lachedamon?

steps.name: Cynisca
steps.text: I cannot make decisions for Lachedamon by myself. However, there is one thing of which I'm sure—

steps.name: Cynisca
steps.text: Lachedamon never turns down a challenge.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: I'll take you across the river, then you should go directly back to Sargon.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Man, I feel like a prisoner being deported—

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Just kidding.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: I understand your friendship towards Minos. But you are still Sargonian, nonetheless.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: And I have a hard time abiding Sargonian feet upon the soil of Minos.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: ...I understand.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: I've been thinking whether there's anything else I can do for Minos, for the mistakes of my forefathers.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Whether I should leave the engineering notes of the Three Poleis and bring only the blueprints back—

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: After all, the padishah only told me to bring back 'blueprints'.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Then I thought, it wasn't enough—it's just a half-hearted compromise, an excuse to run away from my responsibilities and lessen the feeling of guilt.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: I should bring them back and display them in my museum, so that the Sargonians can see it and know that their history books are lying.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Your padishah won't be happy about it.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Who cares? My family wasn't ever particularly good at making the padishahs happy.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Besides, I met with your Astynomos, that shrewd Vulpo, yesterday. I learned that she had already made preparations in advance.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: She had scholars compile and photocopy all the documents and even wrote a paper on it, to be published in a Columbian journal once the exchange was complete and I brought the documents back.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: She asked me to write a foreword, from the perspective of a Sargonian, providing endorsement for the paper.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: And she wanted to leverage the connections I built while studying in Columbia to invite experts to study these invaluable historical records.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: She said she would name me an honorary Minoan for this!

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: ...I admire your courage.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Just doing what my father couldn't.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Besides, I enjoyed my time in Athenius. I went to see the priestess of Endymion Temple yesterday, and she said the vision I saw on stage was a divine revelation!

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: It was a surprise, because the books said Minoan divine revelations only happened in dreams.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Divine revelations can occur in the form of dreams, visions or voices, but dreams are the most frequent form they take, because they are an important way for us to interact with the spirits of the heroes and the departed.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: That's what the priestess said. I told her about the vision I had on the stage, and the dream I had at the burdenbeast ranch. She gave me a very detailed analysis.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Finally she told me, in that solemn and mysterious tone, 'You may not believe it now, Kyría Mashayer, but I believe your revelation is a sign that you will one day become a padishah.'

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: How did she get that? She wasn't messing with me, was she?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: I'm an honorary Minoan now. I'll actually believe what the priestess of Endymion tells me!

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: ...You're free to believe. Divine revelations are simply a form of guidance. Believe in it, and it will bring you strength.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Perhaps a lot of tragedies could have been avoided if a padishah like you ruled over the Sargonian border.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Hm, I think I understand now.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Then I'll take it as a sign of the responsibility I may have to bear in the future—I'll do my best.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: This public announcement... is it a referendum?

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: I'm going back to Athenius after I take you across the river.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: The citizens of Athenius will vote on whether to banish me from the city for my recent actions.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: But you did it for Minos—

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: Regardless of the reason, I must face judgment for my actions. It is the responsibility I must bear.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: It's time. Let's go, Kyría Mashayer.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: I saw Ithakos again in the vision, as well as the river of my homeland.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Was it still red with blood, as it was in your dreams?

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: No, it was quiet and gentle, as I remembered it; not pristine, but carrying the sand and mud that nourishes the soil and life.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: A beautiful revelation. You'll be able to take up poems again, no matter where you go.

steps.name: Xanthos
steps.text: ...Yes.
Whatever the result of the referendum, whether he stays in or leaves Athenius, Xanthos will accept it with grace.
He walks towards the square.
Three months later...

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: Look at this letter from a Lateran scholar—'A most stunning revelation. The study of history is a continuous process of seeking the truth by eliminating misconceptions. I am impressed by the courage that your nation has demonstrated.'

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: And this editorial in a Columbian newspaper—'Sargon shows integrity through proper recognition of history.'

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: I've been calling in favors every single day to repair the damage you've done, ever since that special exhibit that you held after getting back from Minos!

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: I hope you understand that such maverick methods only work once.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: If anything like this happens again, you'd better think about what you'll do once you're removed as curator of the Varjavandabad Museum.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Is this your will, or the padishah's?

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: Is there a difference? My will is the padishah's will.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: I thought we had a consensus before we left Minos—

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: The success of the exchange ceremony and the mission of friendship with Minos is all thanks to your leadership. In turn, it will be your responsibility to explain things to the padishah.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: However much or little you say is entirely up to you, as long as the padishah's happy.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: The exchange ceremony was completed under my leadership to begin with! Besides, how was I to know that you would be so audacious as to...!

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: Don't think you're in the clear just because I smoothed things over for you this time. There won't be a next time.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: Besides, and don't you dare say I didn't warn you—this matter has had a significant impact far and wide. My connections have told me that the City of Gold has sent a herald to Menat-Ha'mait.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: You WILL watch your words and behavior from now on.
I see that news of my mission precedes me.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: S-Such noble elegance and dignity! You must be the herald of the Shahanshah!

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: Your presence honors this humble museum. Have you come to see the exhibits?

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: If you want to see the new special Minoan exhibit, I can...

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: You stay put! I will guide the exalted herald.
The exhibit can wait. I came to communicate the Shahanshah's will.
His Majesty has heard of the mission from Menat-Ha'mait to Minos, and he is most interested.

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: Y-You came to escort me? I-It's my greatest honor!

steps.name: Behnui
steps.text: My family is one of the most honored houses in this land. It was always my greatest dream to serve the Shahanshah in the City of Gold. I knew that one day I would...
It's not you I seek, effendi. Kindly close your mouth, for it is making too much noise.
Medjehtiqedti Nasutu Mashayer. His Majesty awaits your presence in the City of Gold, that the King of Kings might hear of your time in Minos, in your own words.
You should make your preparations quickly. The Shahanshah is eager to hear from you. Do not keep him waiting.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Of course!
